svg.aria-label: Hole-by-hole breadboard map matching a board with column 64 on the left
svg.text: IR sender — holes for your board
Printed column 64 is on the left (Pico / USB). Column 1 is on the right. Unplug USB while inserting parts.
Pico sits in row e and row j. Top rails are + then −. Below row f: + then − at the very bottom.
trench — Pico bridges e (above) and j (below)
row e = Pico pins 40 … 21 (VBUS at col 64, GP16 at col 45)
row j = Pico pins 1 … 20 (GP0 at col 64). IR stays in a–d, to the right of the OLED.
Q1 orange edge = flat, toward the trench
USB on the left, at printed column 64. Pico in row e
and row j. Antenna points right, toward column 45.
e64 = pin 40 VBUS (empty) j64 = pin 1 GP0
e48 = pin 24 GP18 e49 = pin 25 GP19
e46 = pin 22 GP17 e45 = pin 21 GP16
Jumpers above the Pico, then join the long rails:
Leave e64 empty. That pin is 5 V from USB.
a–e in column 48 are already joined to GP18.
a–e in column 49 are already joined to GP19.
On the lower half, j–f in one column are joined.
If your last number is 63 not 64, shift every
hole one column toward the Pico (64→63, …).
Four pins in row a, hanging off the top.
Leave row b under the OLED empty.
3. IR — Q1 is three holes of its own
Do not put the LED or a 15 Ω on B or E.
c26 = C c25 = B c24 = E
LED c28 (A, long) – c26 (K / C, short)
Do not put GND on j31. Those legs are
already joined to e31 inside the switch.
Why the old IR holes failed
The LED, both 15 Ω, and Q1 were stacked on
the same three columns. The middle Q1 leg
(B) often missed c36, so the base sat at
3.3 V instead of ~0.7 V and the LED never
drew current. Q1 now has c26 c25 c24 to
itself. In always-on / carrier ON, B (c25)
must read about 0.7 V, not 3.3 V.
Long LED lead is in c28 (anode).
Column 47 next to GP18 is GND — skip it.
Power is the Pico USB cable. No battery.
